summary: Max Lindenau studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig until 1913.

Historian, Sinologist, and Tibetologist Max Oidtmann earned degrees from Carleton College, Indiana University Bloomington, and Harvard University, studying under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University in Qatar from 2013 to 2021 and became a professor at the University of Munich around 2021.

Philosopher Max Scheler studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1900–1906), University of Munich (~1907–1910), University of Göttingen, and University of Cologne (~1919–1928).

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy Max Walleser studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He founded the Heidelberg Institute for Buddhology in 1928 and taught at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936).
Historian May Oung studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1904 to 1907 and founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Historian Maya Jasanoff studied at Harvard College, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University. She held a position at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a history professor at Harvard University around 2009.
Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, later serving on its General Council from 1964 to 1965.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Mayumi Nasu has held posts at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) as a lecturer and at Koyasan University (attested 2026) as a specially appointed associate professor.

Working in Indology and religious studies, McKim Marriott studied at Harvard University under Clyde Kluckhohn and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he served as professor of anthropology and social sciences from 1953 to 1998.

Buddhist studies and Indology scholar Medawachchiye Dhammajothi studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University. He became a senior lecturer at the University of Colombo around 2000.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

Indologist and philosopher Megumu Honda studied at the Fourth Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and Yale University under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. He later served as professor and professor emeritus at Doho University.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Mei Ching Hsuan earned a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and was attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Meiji Yamada, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962) and served there as a professor (attested between 1963 and 2007).

Linguist and Indologist Meinrad Scheller completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, also studying in Paris. He was a professor at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li, working in Buddhist studies, earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin, working in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Tibetologist and historian Melvyn C. Goldstein earned his BA at the University of Michigan and his PhD at the University of Washington. From 1968 to 2002, he served as a professor in the Department of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University.

Philosopher Merab Mamardashvili studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).
